post.description:
Insert a scene into the storyboard. With ``generate`` (the default) Gemma writes its
keyframe and animation prompts in the background; the scene is returned at once, flagged
``writing_prompts``, and the next run renders only it.

get.description:
What made this take: the prompts saved with it, plus whatever the sidecar manifest adds.

Read on demand rather than on every job fetch — a 40-scene job has hundreds of versions, and
this opens one file.

delete.description:
Drop one keyframe or clip version from a scene's history.

The generated file is kept on disk; only the reference is removed. Deleting the active
version falls back to the newest remaining one (for a keyframe, its clip follows).
Remove a scene and renumber the rest. Its generated files stay on disk unless asked.

(Re)write this scene's prompts from its description with Gemma — for a scene whose
description changed, or whose first write failed.

put.description:
Mark the parts of this scene's frame the animator must not redraw — a brand label, a
monogram — and restore them on the clip that already exists. A paste, not a render.

post.description:
Render a trimmed span to a file and keep it as one of the scene's takes.

A trim in a timeline reaches nothing but `assembly.mp4`. Saved, the cut is a clip like any
other — offered as a take, listed in the version strip, and with `make_active` the scene's
deliverable, so the export folder carries the cut and not the whole render.

Copy a scene's keyframe into the job's project as an asset, so other scenes can use it
as a reference (the picker only offers project assets).

A copy, not a pointer: regenerating the source scene never changes a scene that uses it.
Importing the same frame twice returns the asset already holding those bytes (200).

Ask a running job to stop at its next safe point.

Accepted, not finished: the job keeps status ``running`` with ``stopping: true``
until the worker reaches a checkpoint (a ComfyUI step is withdrawn within a poll
interval; a Gemma call finishes first), then ends ``cancelled`` and can be edited
and resumed with ``POST /retry``.
Resume a failed, stopped or orphaned job from where it stopped; finished work is kept.

post.description:
Add a file to the project. Unless a label was given (a person already named it), the
asset is queued for background description and gets a suggested label when Gemma is done.

Queue assets for background description: unlabelled ones by default, suggested (``auto``)
ones too with ``force``. Labels a person wrote are never touched.

get.description:
A small cached JPEG of the asset for pickers and grids (320 px long side).

A plain ``def`` route: FastAPI runs it in its threadpool, so the one-time ffmpeg call
never blocks the event loop. Built under a temporary name and renamed into place, so a
burst of first requests never serves a half-written file. Assets never change (a new
upload is a new id), so the response may be cached forever. Anything ffmpeg cannot
shrink (already small, not an image) is served as the original file.

patch.description:
Rename an asset's label (e.g. a face as "Maria, age 8") and/or change its kind — labels
and kinds are what the storyboard reads when it assigns identities and references to scenes.

Saving a label marks it ``human``, which both clears the "AI" flag in the UI and makes the
label immune to later descriptions. Confirming an unchanged suggestion is the same call.
Changing the kind rebuilds a still-suggested label for that kind; scenes already using the
asset are not changed.

target_seconds.title: Target Seconds
target_seconds.description: play the KEPT part in N seconds (0.25x-4x of it); omit for natural speed. Trim first, then retime: this measures what start/end kept, not the whole clip.

clip_id.title: Clip Id
clip_id.description: which take from the scene's history; omit for whatever the scene points at now. A scene may be listed more than once, so two takes can be joined into one longer shot.

start.title: Start
start.description: seconds into the clip to start at; omit for the beginning. Snapped to the clip's own frame grid (at 16 fps one frame is 62.5 ms, so 1.234 becomes 1.25).

end.title: End
end.description: seconds to end at; omit for the end. Snapped like `start`.

AssemblySpecIn.title: AssemblySpecIn
AssemblySpecIn.description: All fields optional: omitted items = every clip in order, omitted cuts = fade 0.5s.

AssemblyTakeOut.title: AssemblyTakeOut
AssemblyTakeOut.description:
One render this scene has had. Placing an older take beside the current one extends a shot
with footage already paid for.

ClipOut.title: ClipOut
ClipOut.description: One clip a scene has rendered; the active one is the scene's deliverable.

DeliveryOut.title: DeliveryOut
DeliveryOut.description: A delivery target for this job: what the assembly is rendered as.

JobSpec.title: JobSpec
JobSpec.description:
Request body for creating a job.

The profile (``profile_id`` → project default → built-in default) carries
the generation settings; ``profile_overrides`` deep-merges on top; the
legacy ``evaluate`` / ``face_swap`` / ``max_attempts`` knobs apply only when
sent. ``force`` bypasses a failing environment check.

LockedRegion.title: LockedRegion
LockedRegion.description:
A rectangle of the frame, in fractions of its width/height, whose pixels come from
the keyframe rather than from the model — a brand label, a monogram, an emblem.

A video model redraws every frame from a latent compressed 8x in each direction, so type
below roughly 32 px of cap height cannot survive it. Marking it takes it out of the
model's hands entirely.

ProfileCreate.title: ProfileCreate
ProfileCreate.description: A new user profile: ``base`` (id to start from, default cinematic_16x9) + overrides.

clip_id.title: Clip Id
clip_id.description: which take to cut from; omit for the scene's current clip

make_active.title: Make Active
make_active.description: also make the cut this scene's clip, so the export folder carries it

SaveCut.title: SaveCut
SaveCut.description: Keep a timeline's trim as a real take of that scene.

SaveSceneAsset.title: SaveSceneAsset
SaveSceneAsset.description: Copy a scene's generated keyframe into the job's project, to reuse as a reference.

SceneEdit.title: SceneEdit
SceneEdit.description: One scene's editable fields (storyboard gate review). Index is required.

SceneInsert.title: SceneInsert
SceneInsert.description: Add a scene at ``position`` (0 = first, len = last); Gemma writes its prompts.

SceneOrder.title: SceneOrder
SceneOrder.description: The job's scenes in their new order — every scene's id, exactly once.

SceneRegenerate.title: SceneRegenerate
SceneRegenerate.description:
Redo one scene: ``keyframe`` (everything from the keyframe on) or ``video`` (clip only).
Optional prompt edits are applied first.

animation_negative.title: Animation Negative
animation_negative.default: distorted, morphing, jitter, flicker, extra limbs, warped face

VersionDetail.title: VersionDetail
VersionDetail.description:
What made one keyframe or clip: the prompts recorded with it, plus the sidecar manifest.

The prompts come from the version record (history that outlives the output folder); the
manifest beside the file adds the rest — steps, cfg, model, backend — when it is still there.
